A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reasoning Hijacking and Criteria Attack study. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification attack experiments, cross-model evaluations, ablations, correlation analyses and attention measurements in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds original instruction-adherence, synthetic-data transfer and controlled suffix results in Sections 4.5–4.6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The four-stage criteria-mining, clustering, refutability-selection and suffix-synthesis pipeline remains unchanged, as do the standard attack prompts in Appendix A. Weakened and padded suffixes are introduced as evaluation ablations.

E1.justification: The Enron, Wiki Toxic and IMDb classification coverage remains. V3 adds synthetic-email-to-Enron criteria transfer and canary scenarios within spam detection, including an additional sender-information extraction task (Sections 4.5–4.6; Appendices D–E).

E2.justification: Appendix F/Table 8 adds Pure Lorem Ipsum suffixes at 201 and 402 tokens as evaluated comparison controls. The six prompt-injection baselines in the original comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 adds a distinct instruction-adherence evaluation with four modified trusted prompts, synthetic-only criteria mining using 1,000 balanced emails, and length controls using 201-token padding and 201/402-token noise suffixes. These substantially expand evaluation design; the original sample sets, ASR definition and model/defense settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v3 tests instruction preservation, transfer from synthetic criteria, removal of concluding label assertions and meta-tags, and whether injection length explains success. Sections 4.5–4.6 and Appendix F add substantial evidence addressing central mechanism and robustness questions.

E5.justification: The correlation tests and p-values in Section 5.1/Figure 4 and the existing distribution displays are unchanged. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or statistical testing for the new results.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5 retain their results. V3 adds canary adherence rates of 0.98, 0.76, 0.98 and 0.98 (Table 4), 97.9% ASR under the new synthetic-criteria condition (Section 4.6), and weakened-suffix ASRs of 90.7–92.5% versus 24.2–30.7% for irrelevant-text controls (Table 8).

T1.justification: The operational definition, formal threat model, criteria-bank and refutable-subset definitions, and ASR equations remain unchanged. The synthetic-data scenario is an empirical robustness test; no new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing Reasoning Hijacking and Criteria Attack, and demonstrating vulnerabilities across classification tasks, model backbones and defenses. Added experiments support these retained headline claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds arguments interpreting canary compliance as proof of preserved intent, synthetic transfer as showing independence from distribution matching, and controlled suffix results as establishing a semantic rather than verbosity-driven mechanism. These substantially extend the mechanism and applicability arguments, although the original limitation concerning criteria-bank/distribution matching remains unreconciled.

D1.justification: Appendices D–F supply canary system prompts, the synthetic generation prompt and email categories, the weakened-suffix template, and padding lengths. Existing pipeline prompts, prototype settings and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds five citations and a focused discussion of reasoning-model safety, In-Context Representation Hijacking, Mousetrap, H-CoT and ShadowCoT. It more explicitly positions benign-task black-box injection against safety jailbreaks and training-time backdoors without broadly restructuring the research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized additions expand Section 2.3 and insert Sections 4.5–4.6 and Appendices D–F; the old case-study Appendix D becomes G. Most existing prose and narrative structure remain unchanged, with small terminology and corresponding-author edits.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 4 and 8 and new prompt boxes, relocates Table 2 and Figure 2, and renumbers the retained prototype tables. It also corrects Figure 2's final stage number and explains Table 1's defense abbreviations, while retaining the overall visual design.

improvement.justification: Appendix F addresses directive-wording and injection-length confounds left unresolved by v1, while Sections 4.5–4.6 add useful adherence and transfer evidence. However, the new tests cover one model pair on spam detection, canary adherence is reported without joint attack-success measurements, and claims of definitive proof exceed these measures. The evidence improves, but these limitations temper the overall gain.
